extracted.intended_audience: researchers and organizations seeking CDMRP/DoD biomedical research funding (extramural and intramural applicants)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on eligibility, application submission requirements, and the CDMRP two‑tier review and award-management processes for Congressionally Directed Medical Research Programs funding. Covers procedural registrations, pre-application steps, review criteria (peer and programmatic), consumer involvement, and duplication‑avoidance procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organization eligibility and registration requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: All organizations, including international organizations, are eligible to apply for CDMRP funding opportunities. Specific requirements and focus areas are outlined in funding opportunity announcements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extramural (non-DoD) organizations must be registered with an active status in the System for Award Management (SAM), obtain a Unique Entity Identifier from SAM, and be registered in Grants.gov. In addition, extramural organizations must have a current CAGE code from the Defense Logistics Information Service and an authorized organization representative and business official to submit applications through Grants.gov. Intramural (DoD) organizations may submit full applications to either eBRAP or Grants.gov. All applications must conform to the detailed instructions in each funding opportunity announcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-application submission requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A pre-application must be submitted through eBRAP prior to the pre-application deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must submit the required pre-application through the electronic Biomedical Research Application Portal (eBRAP) at https://eBRAP.org prior to the pre-application deadline; additional submission instruction details are in each Program Announcement or Broad Agency Announcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conformance to funding opportunity announcement instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: All applications must conform to the detailed instructions in each funding opportunity announcement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific requirements and focus areas (including formatting, eligibility, deadlines, and required documentation) are defined in each Program Announcement or Broad Agency Announcement and applicants must follow them exactly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two‑tier review process (overall)
rubrics_metrics.description: CDMRP’s two‑tiered review process: initial scientific peer review followed by programmatic review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modeled after National Academy recommendations, the process combines traditional scientific review strengths with programmatic review focused on relevance to each program’s vision/goals. Once Congress specifies the focus area, CDMRP determines investment strategy and competitively identifies projects for potential funding; applications scientifically peer reviewed first, then undergo programmatic review to select those with the highest merit that best support the program vision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review — scientific and technical merit
rubrics_metrics.description: The peer review is a criteria‑based process where applications are evaluated individually based on their scientific and technical merit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer reviewers (subject matter experts) assess scientific/technical rigor and merit per criteria outlined for the program. Peer review identifies project innovation, duplication and overlap and provides the scientific assessment used in subsequent programmatic comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programmatic review — relevance to program vision and goals
rubrics_metrics.description: Programmatic review compares and selects applications based on how well they support the vision and goals of the specific CDMRP program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During programmatic review applications are reviewed and compared to select those with the highest merit that best support the vision of the program; programmatic reviewers include considerations of program priorities, investment strategy, and impact for Service Members, Veterans, and the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Desired research qualities and selection priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: CDMRP-managed programs share a common goal of advancing innovative, high‑impact ideas, creative solutions, patient care improvements, or breakthrough technologies and resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From small concept awards to clinical trials and collaborative efforts, the CDMRP strives to fund research that is innovative and impactful—targeting projects that can transform healthcare for Service Members and the public. Individual program announcements may further specify desired emphases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consumer involvement in priority‑setting and review
rubrics_metrics.description: Consumers (patients, survivors, family members, caregivers) are included as full voting members in establishing program priorities and reviewing research applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consumers are nominated by community advocacy/support organizations and may serve on scientific peer review panels and programmatic panels; they participate in vision setting, pre-application screening, and programmatic review and bring experiential perspectives, urgency, and passion to discussions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processes to minimize duplication and overlap
rubrics_metrics.description: CDMRP uses a multistep process to minimize research duplication and ensure synergy with other funding efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Steps include: (1) program planning and evaluation of cross-organizational funding landscapes when developing priorities and strategies; (2) requiring applicants to submit a list of past, current and pending funding support at application submission; (3) identification of innovation, duplication and overlap during the two-tier review by peers; (4) submission of updated funding support during award negotiations, certified by the recipient’s Sponsored Programs Office; (5) review of PI-submitted documents and multiple federal/public databases to assess pending/existing support prior to award; (6) technical review of progress throughout the award period including monitoring for overlap/duplication; and (7) coordination with external federal and private funding organizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post‑award monitoring for overlap and progress
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical review during the award period includes monitoring for funding overlap and duplication and assessment of progress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CDMRP conducts ongoing technical reviews of awardee progress to monitor for overlap/duplication with other funding and to ensure project milestones and objectives are being met; findings may affect award management and coordination with other funders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards of reviewer conduct, confidentiality, and COI mitigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer and programmatic reviewers are held to high standards of conduct to ensure credibility, confidentiality, and mitigation of conflicts of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CDMRP takes steps to ensure fair and balanced reviews by subject matter experts and consumers, maintains confidentiality of panel deliberations, and implements policies/processes to mitigate conflicts of interest for reviewers; additional conflict of interest policies are available on the CDMRP website.

rubrics_metrics.name: How applicants learn about funding opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: Announcements and distribution channels for new CDMRP funding opportunities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full details for new opportunities are in Program Announcements or Broad Agency Announcements. CDMRP uses a self-subscription email listserve, posts opportunities on Grants.gov, features them on the CDMRP website, and uses eBRAP; applicants can sign up through CDMRP website or eBRAP or email help@eBRAP.org.
